summary: Fire tower built in 1940 by Fromm Brothers in the town of Corning, Lincoln County, from a dismantled radio tower's steel; listed as gone.

facts.design: Built from the steel framework of a 150-foot radio tower dismantled near Janesville
facts.agency: State conservation department (as named in a January 1940 newspaper item)

events.note: Fromm Brothers, of Hamburg, erected the tower in the town of Corning, per a January 16, 1940 newspaper item
The same item says the Fromm tower brought Lincoln County's number of fire towers to five

evidence.supports: built 1940 by Fromm Brothers of Hamburg in the town of Corning, about 12 miles west of Merrill; steel from a dismantled 150-foot radio tower
evidence.quote: Utilizing the steel framework of a 150-foot radio tower dismantled near Janesville, Fromm Brothers, of Hamburg, have erected a fire tower in the town of Corning, Lincoln county, about 12 miles west of Merrill, where the firm owns a large tract of land.

evidence.supports: state conservation department maintained fire towers in Corning, Rock Falls and Harrison
evidence.quote: Fire towers are being maintained by the state conservation department in the towns of Corning, Rock Falls, Harrison and some in Lincoln county.

evidence.supports: Fromm tower brought Lincoln County's count of fire towers to five
evidence.quote: The Fromm tower in the town of Corning increases the number of fire towers in that county to five.

evidence.supports: Corning listed in Lincoln County as a tower that is gone
separate Fromm entry in Lincoln County, also gone, at different coordinates

notes_for_editor: Corning and Fromm are separate Lincoln County entries on the FFLA list, both marked gone, at different coordinates. The 1940 item places the Fromm tower in the town of Corning, so the two records may be one structure listed twice. No source says so outright, so no correction is proposed; the editor should decide whether to merge the records. No removal date, staffing or design beyond the frame was found. The item is quoted by a transcription page (the page spells the paper 'Wausaw'); the story cites it by date only and the newspaper itself was not checked.
